courses.name: Fair Division
courses.group: Hertz Chair for Algorithms and Optimization (TRA Modelling, chair holder Prof. László Végh)
courses.contents: Course on fair division, offered in Winter 2026/27 under the variable-topic module 'V5C4 Selected Topics in Algorithms and Optimization' (2 SWS, weekly Mon 10:00-12:00, seminar room 1.002, Lennéstraße 2-4). The topic matches the instructor's documented research: algorithmic and game-theoretic fairness notions for allocating indivisible items, in particular envy-freeness up to any item (EFX) and its relaxations, maximin-share guarantees and Nash social welfare. Specific syllabus not published; content areas are inferred from the title and the instructor's publications.
courses.notes: VERIFIED (BASIS WS 2026/27 course catalog, unitId 20939): title 'Fair Division' cross-listed as 'V5C4 / MA-INF 1111' under 'V5C4 Sel Top in Algorithms and Optimization'; Lehrsprache Englisch; Verantwortliche Dr. Hannaneh Akrami; weekly Mon 10:00-12:00, 12.10.2026-01.02.2027, seminar room 1.002 Lennéstraße 2-4. VERIFIED (uni-bonn.de): Hannaneh Akrami is affiliated with the Hertz Chair for Algorithms and Optimization (László Végh, inaugurated April 2025); she spoke at the chair's inauguration symposium on 'Epistemic EFX Allocations Exist for Monotone Valuations' and her 2026 papers (e.g. arXiv:2608.08864) list 'Hertz Chair for Algorithms and Optimization, University of Bonn' as affiliation. Her research is fair division (EFX, MMS, Nash social welfare). INFERRED / NOT VERIFIED: exact event type (BASIS shows no type; 2 SWS weekly in a seminar room under a 'Selected Topics' module suggests Seminar/graduate reading course, could also be labelled otherwise); ECTS (not stated anywhere public yet - for reference, the 2023 module handbook convention is 4 ECTS for 30/33 seminars, but this must NOT be taken as the credit for this new module); detailed syllabus. TRACK RATIONALE: 'AL' because the MA-INF 1xxx code range in the 2023 module handbook belongs to the Algorithms/AL Vertiefungsgebiet and the module sits in the Algorithms & Optimization umbrella of the discrete-mathematics/algorithmic-game-theory environment (Végh/Kesselheim area); still a best guess for a module not yet in the handbook.
